title: Prevent VXLAN VNI reuse causing cross-tenant L2 learning and DNS bleed during peering reconfiguration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers reported intermittent cross-tenant DNS responses and ARP entries immediately following scheduled VPC peering reconfigurations. Investigation shows a race between the peering controller and the overlay reconciler that allowed recently-recycled VXLAN VNI IDs to be learned by the dataplane before the control plane had installed updated isolation ACLs. That transient L2 learning sometimes caused DNS replies to be serviced from the wrong tenant's endpoint, exposing internal hostnames and creating customer-facing failures.

Impact: Affected 4 customers on Dedicated clusters during peering reroutes; symptoms ranged from spurious DNS A responses (wrong source IP) to short-lived connectivity anomalies for services behind private hostnames. Customers observed 10s-60s windows of incorrect resolution after peering swaps; not all requests hit the bad path but enough to trigger escalations from two enterprise customers (FinCo Labs, Acme Health).

Root cause: When a peering is torn down and re-established, the controller reassigns VNIs. Due to VNI ID reuse and an overlay learning process that accepts the first seen MAC/VNI tuple, the dataplane accepted frames on the recycled VNI before the controller pushed the updated per-tenant L2 isolation rules. The reconciler applies ACLs asynchronously; if learning occurs first, the dataplane holds stale forwarding entries until timeout or explicit flush. DNS responses from an adjacent tenant's endpoint were forwarded back into the requesting tenant's subnet.

Mitigation & short-term fix: Implemented emergency control-plane sequenced update: on peering reassign, controller now (a) marks the recycled VNI as quarantined, (b) pushes temporary drop rules to the dataplane to block learning on that VNI, and (c) only then allows the overlay agent to bring the VNI up. This reduces the exposure window to near-zero. Rollout to production Dedicated clusters started 2026-03-05 and completed to 75% of Dedicated fleet by 2026-03-08.

Permanent fix: Change overlay reconciler to treat VNI reuse as a 'cold start' event. New behavior: when VNI ID reappears, dataplane performs deterministic flush of MAC/VNI tuples and requires controller-signed confirmation token before accepting L2 learns on that VNI. Added unit + integration tests and a e2e scenario that simulates peering reassign and validates no learning until confirmation. Target merge: PR #9143. Target rollout: runtime-2.4.

Follow-ups: Add telemetry to surface "VNI-reuse-quarantine" events in Console, add a per-tenant metric for downstream DNS-source-mismatch rate, and update runbooks for on-call to include a faster mitigation (manual quarantine) option.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create two tenants A and B sharing a Dedicated cluster with VPC peering enabled
2) Ensure tenant B hosts an internal DNS responder for a private zone
3) Trigger controller-driven peering reassign that reuses a VNI recently freed
4) Observe overlay agent bringing up VNI; if dataplane learns before ACLs install, DNS replies from B can be forwarded into A
5) Verify the wrong-source DNS response in packet captures and overlay MAC table showing foreign MAC on recycled VNI
mitigations_deployed: 2026-03-05: emergency sequenced update (quarantine then ACLs) pushed to prod Dedicated control plane
2026-03-06: customer communications sent to affected accounts (FinCo Labs, Acme Health) with temporary mitigation and timeline
2026-03-08: mitigation rolled to 75% of Dedicated fleet

2026-03-05 — SRE (Olivia Chen): Emergency rollout started during low-traffic window; monitored error budget and DNS mismatch metric. No regressions observed during initial cohort.
2026-03-07 — Security review (Priya Singh): Reviewed quarantine plan; approved but requested an audit log entry for every VNI-quarantine action. Added to PR.
2026-03-09 — QA (Diego Morales): Integration tests added for token-signed bring-up and deterministic MAC flush; test flake observed due to timing; increased timeouts and made polling idempotent.
